articles.title: AI Automation Cost: Why $0.12 Per Run Can Become $12,000 at Scale
articles.excerpt: Originally published on Soluma AI. One of our workflows cost about $0.12 per prospect across a 500 run test. That is either trivial or a $12,000 decision, depending entirely on the multiplier behind i…
articles.body: Originally published on Soluma AI . One of our workflows cost about $0.12 per prospect across a 500 run test. That is either trivial or a $12,000 decision, depending entirely on the multiplier behind it. One of the most useful lessons we learned about AI cost started with a number that looked almost too small to care about: $0.12. That was roughly what one of our AI workflows was costing to research a prospect . Twelve cents. For a workflow doing real research, that sounded perfectly reasonable, and at small volume it was. Then we did the obvious calculation we probably should all do much earlier when building AI systems. What happens at 100,000 runs? The answer is $12,000. Suddenly, a fraction of a dollar is no longer a technical detail. It is an operating decision.
articles.author: Soluma AI

articles.title: ChatGPT Can’t Backtest: Why “AI” Trading Bots With 10-Year Backtests Are Fiction
articles.excerpt: A bot that needs live ChatGPT calls cannot have a 2019 backtest — ChatGPT didn't exist. That single fact exposes most “AI EAs” on the market. Here is a fact that eliminates most “AI trading bots” on t…
articles.body: A bot that needs live ChatGPT calls cannot have a 2019 backtest — ChatGPT didn't exist. That single fact exposes most “AI EAs” on the market. Here is a fact that eliminates most “AI trading bots” on the market in one sentence: a bot whose decisions require live calls to a language model cannot be backtested — because the model did not exist for most of the backtest window. ChatGPT launched in 2022. A product showing you a flawless 2019 backtest for its “ChatGPT-powered” bot is showing you fiction — or, more charitably, a conventional strategy with AI branding. Real AI decisions require live API connectivity, cost money per call, and take seconds per decision (roughly 3–7 seconds end to end in published breakdowns).
articles.author: Dron Pancholi

articles.title: Building a Medical Investigation AI on an OpenAI-Compatible API
articles.excerpt: November 6, 2026 | 8 min read Most medical AI demos are a chat box with a medical prompt. You send a symptom. You get a paragraph. It can look impressive in a screenshot. Then you try to use it on a r…
articles.body: November 6, 2026 | 8 min read Most medical AI demos are a chat box with a medical prompt. You send a symptom. You get a paragraph. It can look impressive in a screenshot. Then you try to use it on a real case and discover the hard parts: the record is fragmented, the values have dates, the medications interact, the evidence needs a source, and the model has no idea what it does not know. Premedice is a medical investigation AI. The product is built around a different unit of work: the whole case, not the single question. This post is a technical look at how that works, and how to call the API from your own stack. THE PROBLEM WITH A SINGLE PROMPT A standard medical RAG pipeline retrieves a few passages and asks a model to answer. That is useful for general questions.

articles.title: Sell the same key twice, or take money and deliver nothing: the bug every key store must make impossible
articles.excerpt: A digital-goods store can fail in exactly two ways that really matter: It sells the same license key to two people. One of them gets an "already redeemed" error, a refund request and a chargeback. It…
articles.body: A digital-goods store can fail in exactly two ways that really matter: It sells the same license key to two people. One of them gets an "already redeemed" error, a refund request and a chargeback. It takes someone's money and assigns no key at all. That's worse. At Increddy , a storefront for game and software keys, preventing both is the whole job. Here's the problem as a puzzle. Try solving it before you scroll. The puzzle A customer pays. Your backend receives order.placed . Your payment provider sends payment.captured . Either event can arrive more than once , because providers retry by design. They don't always arrive in the order you expect. Each order must end up with exactly one key. Not zero. Not two. What's your design?

articles.body: A disclosed APT vulnerability can let an attacker replace a package that has already been checked with an attacker-controlled package. According to advisories from Debian, Ubuntu and the APT development team, the attacker's code then runs with root privileges when the package is installed. Exposure depends on both download retry settings and the attacker's ability to modify downloaded content. An operating system version alone does not establish whether a machine is affected. Retry settings determine exposure According to Ubuntu, Debian 11 and Ubuntu 20.04 are unaffected in their default configurations. However, the APT development team says user scripts may have enabled Acquire::Retries on these releases.

articles.title: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices
articles.excerpt: Certain configurations of Alpine are affected. Other distros may be as well.
articles.body: Devices running some configurations of Alpine Linux, and possibly other distributions, are affected by a decade-old vulnerability that allows attackers to log into devices with no password. The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine. Further, OpenSSH using musl (pronounced muscle) must not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules), a framework that handles user authentication and account-access checks. Alpine is a lightweight, widely used Linux distribution. Other platforms may be affected if they use the same configurations.

articles.title: 'We got it done!' Spacewalking astronauts finish installing next-gen ISS solar arrays
articles.excerpt: Spacewalkers Anil Menon and Joshua Kutryk installed the final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array on Thursday (Nov. 5), wrapping up a multiyear effort to boost the station's power generation by 30%.
articles.body: Just as NASA is preparing to demonstrate " Max Power " on the ground, two astronauts on a spacewalk have provided the International Space Station (ISS) with the same. Expedition 75 flight engineers Anil Menon of NASA and Joshua Kutryk of the Canadian Space Agency installed and deployed the eighth and final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) on Thursday (Nov. 5), augmenting the space station's legacy solar array wings to produce as much as 30% more electricity. "We got it done!" said Menon at the end of the 6-hour-and-59-minute spacewalk . The EVA (extravehicular activity) began at 8:36 a.m. EST and ended at 3:35 p.m. EST (1336 to 2035 GMT).

articles.title: Andy Weir says his new sci-fi audio drama 'Exoplanet' is a way to 'revive the old art of radio plays' (interview)
articles.excerpt: "Earlier on in my life, even before 'The Martian,' I wanted to bring back audio-only entertainment."
articles.body: Hot off the tremendous theatrical success of this year's "Project Hail Mary," adapted from Andy Weir's 2021 novel of the same name, the New York Times bestselling author is rocketing back into deep space with a brand new Audible Original release landing on Nov. 5, 2026, titled " Exoplanet ." Weir (" The Martian ") is executive producing this ambitious full-cast audiobook drama with acclaimed author and ace comic writer Benjamin Percy ("Wolverine") for the first in a series of curated sci-fi projects for Amazon's Audible. The seven-episode sci-fi thriller stars the vocal talents of Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo in a wild time-travel space disaster odyssey that also benefits from Lucasfilm’s Skywalker Sound, which provided the show’s immersive acoustic elements.

articles.title: Blue Origin announces 3rd stage for its powerful New Glenn rocket —and a new engine
articles.excerpt: Blue Origin has developed a third stage for its New Glenn rocket, which it says will make the launcher even more flexible and capable. The company has also built a new engine, called Northstar.
articles.body: Blue Origin's big rocket is getting a little bigger. Jeff Bezos' company announced today (Nov. 5) that it has developed a third stage for its New Glenn rocket, which it says will make the powerful launcher more capable and flexible. The stage, called the GS3, "enhances New Glenn's capabilities," Blue Origin said in a blog post today . "The third stage enables direct deployment of satellite constellations to GEO [ geostationary orbit ] and supports heavy-lift science and exploration missions to the moon and deep space." Illustration of the variants of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket, with the new GS3 third stage now in the mix. (Image credit: Blue Origin) New Glenn is a two-stage vehicle at the moment.
